oliver: Heads up — HF->Redwood conversion for models/wizard-lite crashed on the fast tokenizer step. The converter error is: 

ValueError: fast tokenizer requires tokenizer.json but none found in model dir.

I only see tokenizer_config.json + vocab/merges files. The loader then quietly falls back to the slow tokenizer, and our evals show a ~4.5% drop on the chat QA benchmark. Anyone seen this exact mismatch? :slightly_frowning_face:

oliver: ls -la model_dir output:
```
-rw-r--r-- 1 oliver staff  345 tokenizer_config.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 oliver staff 52345 vocab.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 oliver staff  234 merges.txt
-rw-r--r-- 1 oliver staff  200 special_tokens_map.json
# no tokenizer.json
```

oliver: command used for onboarding: `python scripts/hf_to_rw.py --src model_dir --out rw_artifact --emit-config`

maya: ugh, this is a fairly common HF friction point. Many HF uploads omit tokenizer.json when the fast tokenizers were never serialized. The HF loader will create a PreTrainedTokenizerFast only if tokenizer.json exists. If not, transformers returns the slow tokenizer class and we get differences in tokenization, esp. for multi-merge BPEs.

sam: two quick options: 1) synthesize tokenizer.json from the slow artifacts (vocab + merges) using tokenizers library and write it into the model dir before conversion, or 2) force the converter to build a Fast tokenizer on the fly via `PreTrainedTokenizerFast.from_pretrained(..., use_fast=True)` with a generated tokenizer JSON. I usually use a small script like this locally:
```
# convert_slow_to_fast.py (sketch)
from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, pre_tokenizers, trainers
from tokenizers.processors import BertProcessing
# load vocab/merges and construct a Tokenizer; dump tokenizer.json
```

sam: I'll push a more complete sketch if you want to avoid manual steps.

oliver: please do — I tried a naive `use_fast=True` and transformers still refused because tokenizer.json missing. A generated tokenizer.json file solves it. I prototyped a quick generator and opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/2745 — it adds `scripts/synthesize_tokenizer_json.py` and a tiny test in tests/tokenizer_tests.py.

ci-bot: CI report for PR #2745: unit tests passed on linux-py310 but failed on linux-py39 due to tokenizers v0.13 api differences. See job logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/2745

maya: thanks, oliver. Plan proposal: (a) merge the synthesize script into our hf->rw conversion pipeline so missing tokenizer.json is auto-generated for supported tokenizers, (b) add a warning metric when a synthesize fallback occurs, (c) add a tiny eval smoke test in onboarding to detect >2% tokenization delta vs a golden tokenization for known prompts, (d) backport to dedicated conversion flow. I can pick (b)/(c) and own the eval harness addition.

oliver: sounds good. For now I ran the script locally, re-ran the conversion, and the fast tokenizer is present in rw_artifact. Re-running the chat QA eval recovered the regression (now within noise). Will attach numbers to the PR.

sam: also worth adding a note in docs/known_hf_gotchas.md about tokenizer.json omission and how to recover. small docs change + the generator should prevent most future hits. :+1:

ci-bot: @oliver CI job re-run queued for PR #2745 (py39 fixed).

oliver: 👍 thanks. Left a TODO to check special_tokens_map parity when synthesizing — we've seen rare cases where the slow artifacts have tokens named differently and that caused off-by-one ids. I'll add that validation to the script.
